title: Kummer and diagonal classes of towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and a scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_{\bullet,T}=((\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_T)_{n\geq1}$ and $A_{\bullet,T}=((\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T)_{n\geq1}$, with quotient transitions, for every scheme $T$ over $S$. Use the topos of inverse systems and its module category $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and its ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $A_{\bullet,T}(1)=(\mu_{\ell^n,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_T}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T)_n$, with the power and quotient transitions; its inverse line tower is denoted $A_{\bullet,T}(-1)$, consistently with [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. The roots of unity and their power transitions are those of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf].

1. In towers of abelian sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ there is a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow(\mu_{\ell^n,S})_n\longrightarrow(\mathbf G_{m,S},(\cdot)^\ell)\xrightarrow{((\cdot)^{\ell^n})_n}(\mathbf G_{m,S},\mathrm{id})\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $\mathbf G_m(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$; the middle tower has power-$\ell$ transitions, and the last tower has identity transitions.
2. A line bundle $L$ (an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]) has its line-bundle class in $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbf Z_S,\mathbf G_{m,S})$. Its constant-tower image has a boundary in $\operatorname{Ext}^2(\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S},(\mu_{\ell^n,S})_n)$ for the sequence in (1), where $\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}$ is the constant tower. This boundary has a canonical coefficient-linear realization
$$R_{\bullet,S}\longrightarrow(\mu_{\ell^n,S})_n[2]$$
in the derived category of $R_{\bullet,S}$-modules in the inverse-system topos: apply derived extension $R_{\bullet,S}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}}-$ to the constant-tower line-bundle morphism $\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}\to\mathbf G_{m,S}[1]$. After forgetting scalars and precomposing with the canonical quotient $\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}\to R_{\bullet,S}$, this morphism is the preceding abelian boundary. Extension along $R_{\bullet,S}\to A_{\bullet,S}$ defines
$$c_1(L):A_{\bullet,S}\longrightarrow A_{\bullet,S}(1)[2]$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(S,\mathcal O_E))$, whose evaluation at $n$ is the finite Kummer first Chern class with coefficients $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$.
3. Put $P=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)=\mathbf P^1_S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $W=P\times_SP$, and let $\Delta:P\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal Cartier divisor, with $\mathcal O_W(\Delta)$ defined by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Put $B=\nu_W^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$ and let $a:B\to\mathbf G_{m,W}$ be the canonical units comparison, induced by restriction to etale charts [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Use the pulled-back Cartier extension $0\to B\to\mathcal M_\Delta\to\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P\to0$ with quotient $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$ for a local equation $t$ [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]. For $C_\Delta=[B\to\mathcal M_\Delta]$ in degrees $-1,0$, write $v:C_\Delta\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P$ for the quotient quasi-isomorphism and $p:C_\Delta\to B[1]$ for the positive projection. Take the image of its connecting morphism $\beta_\Delta=a[1](-p v^{-1}):\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P\to\mathbf G_{m,W}[1]$, using the same cone convention as in (2), and apply the same derived coefficient extension and target identification as in (2) to $\beta_\Delta$. This defines
$$\delta_\bullet:\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P}\longrightarrow A_{\bullet,W}(1)[2]$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(W,\mathcal O_E))$, whose evaluation at $n$ is the finite diagonal class. Its composite with $A_{\bullet,W}\to\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P}$ is $c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$.
4. For $q:P\to S$, let $Rq_{*,\bullet}$ be the proper tower direct image of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The unit and $c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$, where $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is the hyperplane line bundle obtained on affine base opens from [def-pc-projective-space-twist], give an isomorphism
$$b_q:A_{\bullet,S}\oplus A_{\bullet,S}(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{*,\bullet}A_{\bullet,P}.$$
Define the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}:Rq_{*,\bullet}A_{\bullet,P}(1)[2]\to A_{\bullet,S}$ by twisting and shifting $b_q^{-1}$ and projecting onto its second summand. Its evaluation at $n$ is the finite projective-line trace.

proof.text: Kummer exactness on the pro-etale site is a local consequence of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. For a pro-etale object $U\to S$ and $u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$, apply that lemma on the scheme $U$ with exponent $\ell^n$. It supplies an etale cover of $U$ on which $u$ is an $\ell^n$th power. Such a cover is also a cover in the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so the power map on the specified pro-etale units sheaf is an epimorphism. Its kernel is $\mu_{\ell^n}$ by [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Kernels and cokernels of inverse systems are levelwise, as for the system topos in [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. The maps form a sequence of towers because $(u^\ell)^{\ell^n}=u^{\ell^{n+1}}$, and a root of unity maps to its $\ell$th power. This proves (1); no change-of-site identification of the entire units sheaf is being assumed.

source.place: (1); Stacks Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence, applied on every pro-etale object U

proof.text: Construct the integral class of $L$ before introducing finite coefficients. On a Zariski trivializing cover choose frames $e_a$ of $L$ and let its transition units be defined by $e_b=g_{ab}e_a$, so $g_{ab}g_{bc}=g_{ac}$. The section $(u,m)_a$ below is to be read as the frame $ue_a^{m}$ of $L^{\otimes m}$; then $ue_b^m=g_{ab}^mue_a^m$ gives the gluing rule, and this direction of the transitions is the one for which the construction is the class of $L$ rather than of $L^{-1}$. Glue the sheaves $\mathbf G_m\times\mathbf Z$ with abelian group law $(u,m)(v,k)=(uv,m+k)$ by $(u,m)_b\mapsto(g_{ab}^{m}u,m)_a$. The cocycle identity gives the gluing identity; the kernel at $m=0$ is $\mathbf G_m$, and the projection to $m$ is locally split. Thus this explicitly constructs an extension $0\to\mathbf G_m\to E_L\to\mathbf Z\to0$ on the pro-etale site. Its connecting morphism $\lambda_L:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf G_m[1]$ exists and is the extension class by [lem-weil-pbc-ext-one-extension-classification]. Changing frames gives an isomorphic extension fixing endpoints. On the etale site the identical construction is precisely the line-bundle torsor class, by the named construction in [lem-sc-torsor-h1] and the line-bundle/torsor correspondence [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]; both statements allow arbitrary schemes. Hence the pro-etale extension just written fixes the same Kummer sign and convention, without assuming a pro-etale Picard comparison theorem. Taking constant towers is exact (all kernels and cokernels are levelwise), so the constant extension and its connecting morphism define the line-bundle class in the tower category.

source.place: (2), integral line-bundle class; Stacks Tags 03AJ and 06XV

proof.text: Make coefficient linearity part of the construction. Let $\mathscr X$ be the topos of inverse systems of sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ supplied by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on a site presenting this topos to the ring map $\mathbf Z_\bullet\to R_\bullet$. It gives the exact functor $T_R(K)=R_\bullet\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_\bullet}\operatorname{const}(K)$ with values in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_\bullet}(\mathscr X))$, not merely in abelian systems. To check its evaluations, choose a K-flat resolution with flat terms on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The constant-system functor is inverse image of a geometric morphism: it preserves finite limits and is left adjoint to inverse limit. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] it preserves these K-flat resolutions. Constant flat terms remain flat since tensor and exactness of systems are componentwise. Thus a single model $P\otimes R_\bullet$ computes $T_R(K)$ and all evaluations $P\otimes\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. The evaluation isomorphisms commute with transitions because the latter maps are the actual quotient maps in this model.

source.place: (2), derived scalar extension; Stacks Tags 06YY and 0G7E

proof.text: Compute the target of $T_R(\lambda_L)$. After forgetting the new scalar action, resolve $R_\bullet$ by the two-term system $Q_n=[\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf Z]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with transition $(\ell,1):Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. Each term is a flat system (tensor and exactness are levelwise). This bounded complex is K-flat directly: tensoring with any acyclic system is the cone of a map between two acyclic systems, hence acyclic. Therefore the K-flat tensor construction of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes the underlying $T_R(\mathbf G_m)$ by $[\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf G_m]_n$. By step 1 its only cohomology is $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$ in degree $-1$, with transition $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$. Use the positive kernel inclusion $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n[1]\to[\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf G_m]_n$ for this cohomology identification. Define the identification $T_R(\mathbf G_m[1])\simeq(\mu_{\ell^n})_n[2]$ by shifting this identification through the exact functor's shift isomorphism; this fixes its sign. These are identifications inside the module derived category: canonical truncation identifies an object with its unique nonzero cohomology, and [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module] identifies that cohomology's level-$n$ action with its unique $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ action. Also $T_R(\mathbf Z)=R_\bullet$. Apply $T_R$ to $\lambda_L$ to obtain the stated $R_\bullet$-linear Chern morphism.

source.place: (2), explicit two-term computation and power transitions

proof.text: Check the abelian boundary, rather than identifying arbitrary abelian Ext with module Ext. The ordinary tensor units of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] on K-flat resolutions define a natural map from a complex to the scalar-forgotten derived extension: for a K-flat resolution $P\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ use the roof $K\xleftarrow{\sim}P\to P\otimes R_\bullet$; naturality and independence follow from the resolution comparisons in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Check its sign first before shifting. Write $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}M\xrightarrow{f}N\to0$ for the Kummer tower sequence of step 1, so $U=(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$, $M$ has power transitions, and $N$ has identity transitions. Set $C=[U\xrightarrow{i}M]$ and $D=[M\xrightarrow{f}N]$ in degrees $-1,0$. The augmentation $v:C\to N$ is $f$ in degree zero, and the cone projection is $p:C\to U[1]$. With the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], the boundary is $\delta=-p v^{-1}$. Let $a:N\to D$ be the degree-zero inclusion and $j:U[1]\to D$ the positive kernel inclusion. The map $av+jp:C\to D$ is null-homotopic: take the sole nonzero homotopy $h^0=1_M:C^0\to D^{-1}$; then $d_Dh+hd_C$ has components $i$ in degree $-1$ and $f$ in degree zero. Hence $j^{-1}a=-pv^{-1}=\delta$ in the derived category of abelian systems. In the model $N\otimes Q$ of step 4, the tensor unit is precisely $a$. Shift this equality using the target normalization fixed in step 4 to obtain $\delta[1]$ for $\mathbf G_m[1]$. The homotopy is a map of entire systems, since its middle term has the power transitions on both sides. Naturality of the tensor unit gives $\operatorname{Res}(T_R(\lambda_L))\circ(\mathbf Z_\bullet\to R_\bullet)=\delta[1]\circ\operatorname{const}(\lambda_L)$. Thus precomposition with the integral generator realizes the Chern morphism as the boundary in (2). Evaluation gives the identical formula for the finite Kummer boundary, with the same transition $(\ell,1)$ on its two-term models. The scalar-extension adjunction is used in the abelian sheaf setting of steps 2-3, where finite colimits exist; the revised finite-colimit proviso for right exactness imposes no additional hypothesis here.

source.place: (2), replacement for the invalid bare abelian-Ext/module-Ext inference

proof.text: Extend $T_R(\lambda_L)$ along $R_\bullet\to A_\bullet$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], on the same inverse-system topos. This constructs an $A_\bullet$-linear morphism, and evaluation computes finite scalar extension by the K-flat model argument of step 3; the source becomes $A_\bullet$. Apply [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free](1) with $X=S$ and the fixed prime $\ell$ and extension $E$, choosing an auxiliary algebraic closure containing $E$ as in that node's preamble. Its clause (1) supplies one pro-etale cover $\widetilde S\to S$ and generators $\zeta_n$ with $\zeta_{n+1}^\ell=\zeta_n$. The maps $a\mapsto\zeta_n^a$ identify the entire root tower with $R_\bullet$ on that cover: the transition sends $\zeta_{n+1}^a$ to $\zeta_n^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a$ is reduction modulo $\ell^n$. Thus the root tower is locally free of rank one over $R_\bullet$, and tensoring with it is exact because exactness and tensor are computed levelwise. Its derived extension is therefore the degree-zero tower $A_\bullet(1)$, and its dual is the inverse line tower. At each level the finite ring $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ is commutative and killed by $\ell^n$; taking $A=A_n$ and $r=n$ is precisely the finite-coefficient convention of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], where finite discrete coefficient rings have constant coefficient sheaves. Its displayed $B_{E,n}$ is this $A_n$, and its transition $u\otimes a\mapsto u^\ell\otimes\bar a$ is exactly the transition of our $A_\bullet(1)$. The isomorphism of clause (2) of [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free] also identifies any larger annihilating level with this one. No assertion about the integral, rational or algebraically closed bounded constructible categories in that node's revised clause (3) is used. Step 5 evaluated at $n$ is now the finite scalar-extended Kummer class, proving all of (2), with the power transitions on roots and quotient transitions on coefficients.

proof.text:
Fix $W=P\times_SP$ and $F=\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P$. In the current statement of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system], the units in the exact pole extension are $B=\nu_W^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$, rather than the sheaf $G=\mathbf G_{m,W}$ of all pro-etale units. Let $a:B\to G$ be the map adjoint to the identity on units on etale objects, using [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Clause (1) supplies $0\to B\to\mathcal M_\Delta\to F\to0$, with $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$. Put $C_\Delta=[B\to\mathcal M_\Delta]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with quotient quasi-isomorphism $v:C_\Delta\to F$ and positive projection $p:C_\Delta\to B[1]$. By the cone convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] its connecting morphism is $\beta_B=-pv^{-1}$. Define $\beta_\Delta=a[1]\beta_B$. Clause (3) of the diagonal-system statement supplies only the source reduction $T(F)\simeq\Delta_*R_\bullet$ used below. We do not use its target-system identification or clause (4). The target identification for our construction is fixed independently in step 4; the comparison with the finite Cartier class is proved directly in step 8.

Check the normalization directly. Let $\rho:\mathbf Z_W\to F$ send $1$ to $1$ on the diagonal. On etale charts with equations $t_b=g_{ab}^{-1}t_a$, the lifts $s_a=t_a^{-1}$ have ratios $s_b/s_a=g_{ab}$, the transitions of $\mathcal O_W(\Delta)$. The pullback of the pole extension along $\rho$ is locally $B\times\mathbf Z$, with $(b,m)_b\mapsto(g_{ab}^m b,m)_a$; the map to the pole sheaf sends $(b,m)$ to $b t_a^{-m}$. This is an isomorphism onto the pullback: a section over a fixed exponent differs from its chosen lift by a unique section of the kernel $B$. The maps $(b,m)\mapsto(a(b),m)$ define a morphism from this extension to the explicitly constructed full-units extension $E_{\mathcal O_W(\Delta)}$ in step 2. They commute with the transitions because $a(g_{ab})=g_{ab}$, and have endpoint maps $a$ and the identity of $\mathbf Z$. Naturality of connecting morphisms, or the commuting maps of the two cones with their negative projections, gives $a[1]\beta_B\rho=\lambda_{\mathcal O_W(\Delta)}$. The endpoint convention is the one in [lem-weil-pbc-ext-one-extension-classification]. No isomorphism $B\simeq G$ is assumed.

Apply the module-valued exact functor $T_R$ of step 3 to this corrected integral morphism, using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The underlying source reduction is the cited $T(F)$, and it has only degree-zero cohomology $\Delta_*R_\bullet$. Truncation inside the module derived category and the unique levelwise quotient actions of [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module] identify the source there. Identify the target with $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n[2]$ using exactly the positive-kernel identification and shift normalization of step 4; do not alter that identification for the supported class. This produces the $R_\bullet$-linear supported morphism $T_R(\beta_\Delta)=-T_R(a[1])T_R(\partial)$, where $\partial=pv^{-1}$ is the cited positive roof with target $B[1]$. Applying the additive functor to the preceding integral equality shows that its composite with $R_{\bullet,W}\to\Delta_*R_{\bullet,P}$ is the Chern morphism of $\mathcal O_W(\Delta)$. All maps are constructed on entire systems before evaluation.

proof.text:
Extend the corrected map $T_R(\beta_\Delta)$ from $R_\bullet$ to $A_\bullet$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3), $\mathcal O_E$ is finite free over $\mathbf Z_\ell$; a fixed basis reduces to compatible bases of $A_n$ over $R_n$. Thus $A_\bullet$ is finite free over $R_\bullet$, and its tensor functor is exact levelwise. In such a basis the canonical map $A_\bullet\otimes_{R_\bullet}\Delta_*R_\bullet\to\Delta_*A_\bullet$ is the identity on the corresponding finite direct sum of copies of $\Delta_*R_\bullet$. Step 6 identifies the target as $A_\bullet(1)[2]$. Define $\delta_\bullet$ by this extension, retaining the source and target identifications of step 7.

At level $n$ this construction is the connecting boundary of the pole extension followed by finite Kummer reduction and coefficient extension. Indeed step 5's natural tensor-unit calculation applies to the integral morphism $\beta_\Delta:F\to G[1]$: its scalar-forgotten reduction, precomposed with $F\to F\otimes^L R_n$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{Kum},n}[1]\beta_\Delta$. The source is the ordinary quotient $F\otimes R_n=\Delta_*R_n$, by step 7's source calculation. This is precisely the boundary construction of the finite Cartier class in the source sk-lem-geo-cartier.proof.md, (G1), with the same connecting-map convention; here $\beta_\Delta$ is the image under $a[1]$ of the actual pulled-back connecting boundary. The naturality and target comparison are verified below. Step 7's explicit pullback equality, after these two additive coefficient extensions, gives $\delta_\bullet\circ(A_{\bullet,W}\to\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P})=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. Apply the current statement of [sk-lem-geo-cartier] with $r=n$, $R=R_n$, $\Lambda=A_n$, $Z=W$ and $D=\Delta$. Its coefficient hypothesis holds: $A_n$ is a finite commutative $R_n$-algebra killed by $\ell^n$, including when $E$ is ramified. Use the compatible standard charts of [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] with $r=1$; [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] identifies its underlying scheme with our $P$. Over $\operatorname{Spec}(C)\subset S$, the degree-zero localizations are $C[T_1/T_0]$ and $C[T_0/T_1]$. The diagonal is effective Cartier over arbitrary $S$: on the same affine chart its equation is $x-y$, and on opposite charts it is $xy-1$. Multiplication by $x-y$ is injective by division by the monic polynomial in $x$; if $(xy-1)f=0$, comparing constant terms and then successively coefficients gives $f=0$. These charts cover $W$.

The current Cartier statement defines its finite twist and Chern class by etale construction followed by comparison inverse image. Write $\nu:W_{\mathrm{proet}}\to W_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The extension used in step 7 is already the exact inverse image of the etale pole extension, as specified by the current diagonal-system statement. Apply the exact-inverse-image naturality in [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] with modulus $\ell^n$ to that extension. On the etale site units are $\ell^n$-divisible by the arbitrary-base Kummer lemma used in step 1; this remains true of $B$ under exact inverse image. Multiplication by $\ell^n$ on $F$ is injective, also following from step 7's source-reduction calculation. Thus derived reduction of $\beta_B$ is the comparison pullback of the etale supported boundary, with the positive-kernel/negative-connecting normalization of steps 4-5. It is the whole supported morphism that naturality compares. For the integral supported quotient the canonical map $\nu_W^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathbf Z_P\to\Delta_{\mathrm{proet},*}\mathbf Z_P$ is the mate of the inverse-image square and the closed counit in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], with discrete coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$. Its local formula is $m\mapsto m$, and it is the identification in the pulled-back extension. This uses exact inverse image on abelian sheaves, not the finite-ring module assertion of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] with integral coefficients.

To pass from $\beta_B$ to $\beta_\Delta=a[1]\beta_B$, note that $a$ commutes with every power map. The Kummer diagrams therefore give a map from the pulled etale root sheaf to the full pro-etale root sheaf. Tensor on the same two-term resolutions of step 4 shows that this is the cohomology map of $T_R(a)$; it respects the positive kernel inclusions and all power transitions. Consequently the normalized target map is exactly that roots comparison, rather than an arbitrary change of sign.

On the reduced target the comparison $\nu^{-1}\mu_{\ell^n,\mathrm{et}}\to\mu_{\ell^n,\mathrm{proet}}$ is an isomorphism. Indeed the etale rank-one trivialization in [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], applied to $N=\ell^n$ and $A=R_n$, gives local generators, and the map sends each generator to itself. The same finite etale covering is a pro-etale covering, where both sheaves identify with the constant $R_n$ and the map is the identity. Constant rings and exact comparison inverse image are supplied by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. For the source use [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] with $g=\Delta$ and the degree-zero etale sheaf $R_{n,P}$; $\Delta$ is a closed immersion, hence finite, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The etale direct image is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], so the comparison gives $\nu^*\Delta_{\mathrm{et},*}R_{n,P}\simeq R\Delta_{\mathrm{proet},*}R_{n,P}$. Taking degree zero identifies the right side with ordinary $\Delta_*R_{n,P}$: for a nonnegative injective resolution $I$ it is $\ker(\Delta_*I^0\to\Delta_*I^1)=\Delta_*\ker(I^0\to I^1)$ by left exactness. This degree-zero comparison is the adjunction map just specified, reduced modulo $\ell^n$: both are the mate of the same inverse-image square and closed counit. The cited theorem preserves the adjunction unit, so this is the supported-constant comparison used in the current Cartier statement. Monoidality of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] commutes these comparisons with extension to $A_n$. Consequently evaluation of our constructed map is the finite Cartier morphism constructed from (G1) and transported by $\nu^*$, with exactly the twist, supported source and positive Chern normalization in the current statement. Its coefficient and Cartier-preserving base-change assertions therefore apply. This establishes clause (3) by the actual supported boundary construction; it does not infer equality of supported maps merely from their composites with the coefficient unit. This argument uses [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system] only for its pulled extension and source reduction, not for its target identification or clause (4). In particular at $S=\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\mathbf F}_2$, $\ell=3$, $E=\mathbf Q_3$, $n=1$, restriction to $P\times\{y\}$ gives $+c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$, with fibre trace $1$ by [det-sp-p1-trace](2); the uncorrected positive roof would give trace $-1=2$ in $\mathbf Z/3$.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] with the two-element index set $\{0,1\}$, $q:P\to S$ is proper. Use its compactification $q=q\circ\mathrm{id}_P$ when applying [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The coefficient sheaf and its twists and shifts are bounded below, as required by that node's $D^+$ hypothesis. Use the canonical ringed-topos derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] for the levelwise morphism of inverse-system topoi induced by q. The hyperplane line on each affine base open is [def-pc-projective-space-twist] with $d=1$: its frames satisfy $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$. These transition functions commute with restriction on the base, so they glue to the specified $\mathcal O_P(1)$. Form $b_q$ by the tower adjunction unit and the adjoint of the Chern morphism of $\mathcal O_P(1)$, untwisted and shifted on its source. Clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] supplies the bounded-below direct-image comparison. To check evaluation of the actual adjunction maps, apply [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] with the strict coefficient system $B_n=(A_n)_S$ and the pro-etale inverse image of $q$. The pulled-back coefficient system is $(A_n)_P$, since inverse image preserves constant sheaves. This lemma explicitly preserves evaluation, units, counits, tensor products and adjunction transposes, so the constructed tower unit/Chern map evaluates to the same map over $A_n$. The canonical identification of the pulled-back twist with the twist on $P$ follows from the single compatible-generator cover of step 6: its pullback sends each generator to the same root and the local coefficient-line identification to the identity. No unrestricted projection-formula isomorphism from clause (2)(a) is used. For completeness this finite map is invertible without imposing Noetherianity on $S$. Apply [det-sp-p1-trace](1) over $R_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. On restricting $A_n$-modules to $R_n$, $A_n$ is a finite direct sum of $R_n$ using the basis in step 8. Canonical composition of ringed-topos derived direct images [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] applied to the two factorizations of the coefficient-change square identifies restriction of $Rq_{*,A_n}$ with $Rq_{*,R_n}$ of restriction; exact restriction is its termwise derived functor, as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](4). Thus the restriction of $(b_q)_n$ is the direct sum of these $R_n$ projective-line isomorphisms: on the $j$th basis vector its Chern component is $e_j\otimes c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ by step 6, and its unit component is $e_j$ times the unit. Finite direct sums commute with an additive derived direct image. Since restriction does not change cohomology sheaves it reflects isomorphisms. Hence $(b_q)_n$ is invertible over $A_n$. Finally [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](3) implies $b_q$ is invertible in the tower module derived category. For this use of clause (4), the underlying sheaf category is abelian and its tensor is additive; the finite-colimit existence condition in the revised clause (2) is therefore satisfied.

proof.text:
Put $V=A_{\bullet,S}(1)[2]$, an invertible object with inverse $V^{-1}=A_{\bullet,S}(-1)[-2]$ by step 6. Write $L=q^{-1}$ and $R=Rq_{*,\bullet}$ for the derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; its pullback tensor comparison gives $L(V^{-1})=(LV)^{-1}$. For any $M$ and $C$, tensoring by these inverse lines and applying that adjunction gives natural bijections
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(M,RC\otimes V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes V^{-1},RC)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LM\otimes LV^{-1},C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LM,C\otimes LV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,R(C\otimes LV)).
$$
The forward map is the counit-tensor transpose specified in the cited node: transpose, cancel the inverse line and transpose back. Running these bijections backwards gives its inverse; their composites are identities by the evaluation/coevaluation cancellations for the line and the adjunction triangle identities. Thus the projection map is invertible for this $V$ over the arbitrary scheme $S$, without applying the restricted general projection theorem of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2)(a). Take $C=A_{\bullet,P}$ and use $LV=A_{\bullet,P}(1)[2]$ from the generator calculation in step 9. Tensor $b_q$ with $V$ and compose with this projection isomorphism to obtain $A_{\bullet,S}(1)[2]\oplus A_{\bullet,S}\simeq Rq_{*,\bullet}(A_{\bullet,P}(1)[2])$. Define $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}$ to be the second projection after its inverse. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], evaluation preserves the tensor, counit-tensor transpose, adjunctions and compositions in this construction, and it preserves inverses by functoriality. The evaluated splitting is therefore precisely the twist of the finite unit/Chern splitting, so [det-sp-p1-trace](2) identifies its second projection with the finite trace, extended to $A_n$. This proves (4) with the stated trace type.
